name: Short Put Calendar Spread (Reverse Put Calendar)
summary: Buy the near-term put and sell the longer-dated put at the same strike; the put mirror of the reverse calendar, profiting from a large move or a drop in back-month IV, naked after the front expires.
max_profit: Approximately the net credit received, when the underlying ends far from the strike in either direction at front expiry.
max_loss: UNDEFINED in practice. Worst case before front expiry is a pin at the strike; after front expiry the naked short put's maximum loss is (strike x 100 - credit) per contract if the underlying goes to zero.
breakevens: Two, outside of which the trade profits: approximately strike +/- (1.0 to 1.3) x the credit in underlying points at front expiry.
when_to_use: Same regime as the reverse call calendar: steep contango (back_IV - front_IV >= 5 vol points) with IV rank > 60, or ahead of an anticipated volatility expansion in the near term. Rarely the best expression of that view.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4 - the later-expiring short put is uncovered once the front long put dies. The automation must reject this structure at level 3.
back_IV - front_IV >= 5.0 vol points AND IV rank > 60.
Front 14-30 DTE, back 45-90 DTE, same strike, ATM by delta 0.45-0.55.
Credit >= 20% of the back-month put premium.
Underlying must be one you would tolerate owning 100 shares of at the strike (the naked-put tail is real).
Size assuming cash-secured equivalent: strike x 100 of exposure per contract.
management_rules: Close if back-month IV rises 5 vol points above entry.
Never let the front long put expire while the short back put is open.
exit_rules: Close the entire structure no later than 5 trading days before the FRONT (long) leg expires.
Close the short put immediately if |delta| >= 0.85 or extrinsic <= $0.10 (interest-driven early exercise window on deep-ITM puts).
When legging out, buy back the SHORT put first.
At level 3, reject at entry - there is no valid management path.
assignment_risk: The short leg is the long-dated one, so exposure lasts months and outlives the hedge. Assignment delivers +100 shares at the strike, requiring strike x 100 of buying power. Deep-ITM short puts are exercised early for interest carry, particularly when rates are elevated.
buying_power: Naked short put margin: greater of 20% of underlying value minus OTM amount or 10% of the strike, plus premium. Typically $1,500-$8,000 per contract.
common_mistakes: Assuming defined risk; holding past front expiry; using it to express a 'crash' view when a long put or put backspread is cleaner; ignoring hard-to-borrow names where early exercise is far more likely.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
